Profile
Research/Clinical Interests
Dr. Henry's research interests include head and neck cancers, soft-tissue sarcomas, DNA damage response mechanisms and homologous recombination deficiency, and feline oncology.
Education
2019-2022: Cornell University, Resident in Radiation Oncology
2016-2019: Cornell University, Resident in Medical Oncology
2013-2014: University of Pennsylvania, Intern in Small Animal Medicine and Surgery
2013: Ross University School of Veterinary Medicine, Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (Honors)
Biography/Professional Experience
Dr. Henry is a graduate of Ross University’s School of Veterinary Medicine. He completed an internship in small animal medicine and surgery at the University of Pennsylvania. Following his internship, he worked as an emergency medicine veterinarian prior to returning to Cornell University in 2016 to complete residencies in both medical and radiation oncology. Dr. Henry is a board-certified diplomate of the American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine (Oncology) and the American College of Veterinary Radiology (Radiation Oncology).
Dr. Henry has special interest in canine and feline head and neck tumors, non-surgical sarcomas, DNA damage response mechanisms, homologous recombination deficiency, and feline radiobiology.
